title: Node.js Event Loop: Why Non-Blocking Wins

scenes.say: Ever wondered why Node.js apps handle tons of requests without freezing up? Let's see what keeps things moving.

scenes.label: EventLoop
scenes.sub: The event loop lets Node.js run code, handle events, and process I O—all without blocking.
scenes.say: The secret is the event loop. It lets Node run code, handle events, and process input and output, all without blocking.
The event loop moves through phases: timers, input and output, immediate callbacks, and cleanup. Each phase handles a different kind of task.

scenes.title: libuv Offloads Work
scenes.say: Heavy tasks, like reading big files, get offloaded to a background thread pool by libuv. When they're done, the event loop picks up the callback.

scenes.question: Is Node.js always non-blocking?
scenes.right: Nope. Synchronous code or heavy loops can still block everything.
scenes.say: Here's a common trap: People think Node is always non-blocking. But if you run slow, synchronous code, the event loop still gets blocked.
